answer.rationale: Objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so the response to the competitor's price cut should defend value delivery rather than match price. Only two directions rest on recovered primary evidence this cycle: exp_86 (shortened onboarding: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) and exp_91 (activation messaging: engagement +11%, activation +6%, retention +1%). Onboarding simplification has the stronger retention and time-to-value effect, which is the mechanism most likely to blunt price-driven churn by making the product's worth evident before the renewal decision. Promotional pricing is explicitly excluded: memory_73 records that it lifts acquisition and revenue but materially reduces 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it — under acute churn pressure it would convert a retention problem into a margin-plus-retention problem, and the urgency of the competitor announcement is exactly the condition under which that warning is most likely to be rationalized away. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are plausible but unverified this cycle and neither targets the price-sensitive SMB accounts now churning; enterprise assist also aims at a different segment entirely. Caveats preserved rather than collapsed: exp_86's lift was measured in a normal competitive environment, not under an active deeper price cut, so the retention effect may not transfer at the same magnitude to accounts already in churn conversations; memory_31 (signup-field reduction) is a distinct, unverified claim and should not be silently merged into the onboarding case. Because the evidence is confirmed but the context has shifted, I am running this as a standard experiment with retention and time-to-value as primary readouts, not a broad rollout, and I am queuing memory_31, memory_73, memory_57 and memory_44 for verification when archive access returns next week. Downstream risk flagged: if a shortened-onboarding win is reported without the context caveat, later sessions may treat it as a general answer to price competition, which it is not.
